title: any vs unknown in TypeScript
caption:
Everyone reaches for any when TypeScript gets in the way. Seniors reach for unknown. Which one are you?

TypeScript quizzes and coding tasks on devShark: devshark.app 🦈

slides.headline: any vs unknown.
slides.body: Both accept [[every value]]. Only one keeps you safe.

slides.headline: any turns checks off.
slides.body: Call anything on it and the compiler [[stays quiet]], until it breaks at runtime.

slides.headline: unknown makes you check.
Prefer [[unknown]].
slides.body: Narrow it with typeof, instanceof or a type guard before you use it.

title: 401 vs 403
caption:
401 or 403? Interviewers love this one, and plenty of seniors still swap them. Do not be one of them.

Interview prep for web developers on devShark: devshark.app 🦈
#interviewprep #http #webdevelopment #backend #devshark

slides.headline: 401 or 403?
slides.body: Both say [[no]]. They mean different things.

slides.headline: 401: who are you?
slides.body: The request has [[no valid credentials]]. Log in and try again.

slides.headline: 403: not allowed.
slides.body: The server knows who you are, but you [[lack permission]]. Logging in again will not help.

slides.headline: 401 is authentication. 403 is authorization.
slides.body: Despite its name, 401 Unauthorized is about [[who you are]].

title: Use a button, not a div
caption:
That div with onClick works fine. For you. Want to build for everyone? Learn it step by step on devShark: devshark.app 🦈
#accessibility #a11y #react #frontend #devshark

slides.headline: Use a button.
slides.body: A div with onClick [[looks the same]] but works for fewer people.

slides.headline: The risky one
slides.body: No focus, no Enter or Space, [[no role]] for screen readers.

slides.headline: The right one
slides.body: Focus, keyboard and role [[come for free]].
